proposals.evidence: DEDR3213 gives Tamil tiṅkaḷ, Malayalam tiṅṅaḷ, Kannada tiṅgaḷ, Kodagu tiŋga and Tulu tiṅgoḷu month. The selected simple southern survey tiŋga/tiŋa/tīŋgala responses are comparative lect extensions of this month family, preserving shortening and final-vowel notation. This is a comparative family proposal; inheritance versus local transmission in this survey lect remains subject to review.

proposals.evidence: DEDR5422 gives Gondi vil and Malayalam vil/villu bow, with Tamil vil. The simple survey rainbow nouns are proposed as a semantic extension bow → rainbow within this family; the southern minority-lect matches are comparative. This does not analyse the longer named-bow compounds, and DEDR itself supplies bow rather than the survey rainbow sense. This is a comparative family proposal; inheritance versus local transmission in this survey lect remains subject to review.

proposals.evidence: DEDR183 explicitly gives Irula amme father, distinct from the mother sense in several other languages. The survey Irula amma/ammæ/amman variants are compared within that documented father usage, preserving vowel and final-n variation. Nursery-word resemblance alone does not establish a unique historical transmission route. This is a comparative family proposal; inheritance versus local transmission in this survey lect remains subject to review.

proposals.evidence: DEDR156(a) gives Tamil appaṉ, Malayalam appan, Kannada appa and Kodagu appë father. The selected survey appa/appan/appe responses retain the same locally elicited father sense; minority-lect extensions are comparative. This nursery/honorific family does not by itself distinguish shared inheritance from regional diffusion, and other languages’ mother/aunt senses are not substituted. This is a comparative family proposal; inheritance versus local transmission in this survey lect remains subject to review.

proposals.evidence: DEDR4395(a) gives Tamil peṇ woman/female, peṇṭu woman/wife, Malayalam peṇ and Kannada peṇṇu/peṇḍa woman. The selected simple southern survey forms are comparative lect extensions within this family; final vowels, gemination and retroflex stops remain as recorded, with no substitution of the marriage sense of other branches. This is a comparative family proposal; inheritance versus local transmission in this survey lect remains subject to review.
